newsitem.title: USA: U.S. concerned over Turkish naval exercises.
newsitem.headline: U.S. concerned over Turkish naval exercises.

text.p: The United States urged eastern Mediterranean countries on Wednesday to avoid "provocative military initiatives" after Turkey sent warships and submarines to northern Cyprus for naval exercises.
"The United States is concerned," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.

"We believe that all countries in the eastern Mediterranean, including Turkey, have a self-interest now -- just before the commencement of the UN-sponsored talks on July 9 -- not to undertake any provocative military initiatives that undermine confidence, that get people excited, that undermines stability in the eastern Mediterranean," he said.
Burns said Turkey told Washington this was a "naval visit and...routine...not military exercise, but port visits in Cyprus. And the Turks say this is periodic and not unusual."

But he said that Turkey and other countries in the region needed to be "more transparent" and to tell other countries affected -- in this case Greece and the Greek-led Cypriot government -- what it was doing.
Cyprus on Tuesday said it would protest to the United Nations against the arrival of the six Turkish warships and three submarines in northern Cyprus.

The protest would also concern infringement of the Nicosia flight information region, an area administered by the Cyprus civil aviation department, by 16 Turkish F-16s on Sunday and Monday, the government in Nicosia said.
The flotilla is to depart on June 20.

Cyprus has been divided since Turkey invaded in 1974 after a short-lived coup in Nicosia backed by the military junta then ruling Greece. A self-declared Turkish Cypriot state in the north is recognised only by Turkey.

The leaders of the island's Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities are due to embark on a new round of United Nations-sponsored direct talks in New York on July 9 in an attempt to bridge differences between the two sides.
